In the 1960s, a 5 year old, Jeryl Lynn came down with this disease. Her father rushed to her bedside and cultured the causal virus from her throat. The attenuated virus strain he created is still the primary component used in vaccines worldwide today

The first recorded clinical description of this disease was by Hippocrates where he described large, soft swellings near the ears on one or both sides of the face. Some male patients also suffered from painful swelling of the testicles and many patients experienced a dry cough and hoarseness.

This was discovered by an inexperienced pharmaceutical team in the early 1980s. The breakthrough moment actually came when an inexperienced team member accidentally gave a rat a massive dose of a compound they were testing. His team member shared 'it was like adding the animal to the drug instead of adding the drug to the animal', but this accident helped them continue work developing this drug

Once this drug is swallowed, the liver converts a good portion to an active metabolite called EXP3174. This metabolite is 10 to 40 times more potent at blocking AT1 receptors than the parent drug, relaxing arterial and venous smooth muscle and dilating efferent arterioles in the kidneys more than afferent.

It is now in the top 10 most commonly prescribed medications in the United States and valued at 1.5 billion dollars globally. Unlike a similar medication, this medication does not affect bradykinin and does not cause patients to cough

In 1905, this was discovered by Dr. Darling during an autopsy where he noticed small intracellular bodies inside cells. He named it 'tissue-lover with a capsule' and for years, the condition was known as 'Darling's disease'
In 1997, Bob Dylan was hospitalized with severe chest pain and doctors discovered he was suffering from pericarditis caused by this dimorphic fungus.

Skin-test surveys revealed that up to 80% of adults living in the Mississippi basin had calcified lung scars, meaning they had encountered the fungus and built natural immunity without ever realizing it was a serious disease.
